# Historical execution audit

**Provenance.** Let `P` denote `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/`. Expanded files cited below are under `P/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C1/`. Their archive is `P/work/scene_archive/bundles/r1--sceneevolve_cli.tar.gz`; each corresponding member is `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C1/` plus the cited relative file path. References give source IDs and original line numbers. No images were supplied for visual inspection.

## Shipboard development scene

The step-3 code describes adjustments after a step-2 render: move furniture and the column, expose the bench and ventilator, and darken the deck and rear lighting. These are the author's comparison and intentions, not independent visual findings (X0776, `development/commons_118588033/steps/003/build.py`, lines 4–10).

The scene uses boxes and rods for compartment architecture, a two-color column, three-tier bunks, lockers, benches, machinery, chair, ventilator, fittings, pipes and pendant lamps (X0776, lines 31–102, 104–200, 202–272). The chair back is rotated 12 degrees. Camera position is `(0.35, -3.5, 1.64)`, target `(-0.10, 4.3, 1.62)`, lens 32 mm, sensor 36 and vertical shift −0.08. Three pendant area lights and a foreground fill are specified, along with world strength 0.18 and AgX (X0776, lines 12–15, 173–180, 274–292, 332). Materials use supplied colors; the script sets mesh-material roughness to 0.43 and conditionally copies and gives lamp-disc materials emission strength 3. It contains no image-texture operation (X0776, lines 300–330).

The result reports `ok: true`, no error or stderr, Blender 4.2.10 LTS completing 16 samples and saving both PNG and blend file (X0777, `development/commons_118588033/steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7). The task records a **384 × 512 reference**, not independently measured output dimensions (X0778, `development/commons_118588033/task.json`, lines 2–5). No selection or acceptance record for this scene is supplied.

## Kitchen corner selection

Step 3 explicitly responds to perceived pale surfaces and low sink/faucet placement. Its model combines box walls, 31 tilted blind slats, a framed cabinet, towel ring, sink and faucet, pitcher and utensils. The sink “basin” is a shallow dark filleted box, not a modeled recessed cavity. The blender cup is a subtraction of two rods; the pitcher has separately modeled lid and handle (X0787, `selection/commons_133800864/steps/003/build.py`, lines 5–10, 28–87, 107–184). A 64-segment ring mesh forms the jug, while a 32 × 45 grid with solidify and subdivision forms the towel; a FONT object supplies “FILTER” (X0787, lines 263–289, 303–337).

Color-matched node edits add object-coordinate noise/ramp stone, metallic chrome, transmissive cup material, window emission and paper bump; towel noise drives a separate bump (X0787, lines 219–261, 291–301). The step-3 camera is at `(-1.55, -2.45, 1.99)`, target `(-0.07, 0.12, 1.66)`, 50 mm; two area lights, world strength 0.18, AgX and exposure −0.35 are specified (X0787, lines 17–19, 339–354).

Steps 1–3 each report successful Blender renders, empty stderr, 16 samples and saved PNG/blend outputs (X0784, `selection/commons_133800864/steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7; X0786, corresponding `steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7; X0788, corresponding `steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7). `selected.json` records step 3, although the record's `selected` field is null (X0781, `selection/commons_133800864/selected.json`, line 2; X0780, corresponding `record.json`, line 57). The record says valid and functional pass, with overall 0.5006; its checks concern structural/edit operability, while semantic completeness and support/collision truth are null (X0780, lines 16–34). This is not independent visual-quality validation.

## Modern kitchen selection

The supplied step-3 build describes darkened rear cabinetry, an island, layered sink, extractor, red kettle, posts and exposed ceiling, mostly assembled from boxes with rods, a ball and swept tubes (X0790, `selection/commons_138420790/build.py`, lines 5–11, 37–183). The code matches realized mesh world-space bounds against recorded box centers and sizes to assign explicit finishes, then applies procedural longitudinal noise, ramp and bump to matched posts. That matching is a material-assignment technique, not proof of physical contact (X0790, lines 185–255).

The coded camera is `(4.10, -6.50, 2.30)` toward `(-0.82, 0, 1.50)`, lens 48 mm; four area emitters, world strength 0.18 and AgX are specified (X0790, lines 13–15, 257–276). Step 1 demonstrably rendered successfully with 16 samples and no stderr (X0795, `selection/commons_138420790/steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7). The record reports three executions, completion without runtime error, valid and functional passes, and overall 0.4339; step 3 is recorded in `selected.json`, while the record's `selected` field is null (X0791, `selection/commons_138420790/record.json`, lines 16–34, 37–53, 57; X0792, corresponding `selected.json`, line 2). No individual step-3 result log is supplied.

**Limit:** Coordinates, constructed meshes and pass flags establish neither part contact nor fidelity to the reference. These are completed reported runs, not evidenced technical rendering failures; without the images, their reconstructions could nevertheless be visually poor.
